pr_title: Revert fix for on_failure_callback when task receives a SIGTERM
pr_body:
From the comment on exception handling when a task is killed externally we do not handle callback thus
the above fix was made in error. Here's the comment on code:

 for case when task is marked as success/failed externally
 or dagrun timed out and task is marked as skipped
 current behavior doesn't hit the callbacks

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/b65dbaaf3f21ea5396da121bbfa7f895d0ab8516/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1468-L1470

closes: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/30146
pr_comments:
> Revert sounds like the right choice to me.
> 
> I think it could be nice to add the test cases from: #30146 to prevent similarly bad changes being introduced in the future. But maybe that is better done in a followup PR.

Feel free to make the PR once this is merged. Also we can add a comment on the signal handler itself to say that we don't handle callbacks when tasks are marked failed externally

> Also we can add a comment on the signal handler itself to say that we don't handle callbacks when tasks are marked failed externally

Good idea. I think that's the super-easy (though temporary) fix.

issue_context.title: on_failure_callback call multiple times and when task has retries
issue_context.body:
### Apache Airflow version

2.5.2

### What happened

The changes in https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/29743 adds a new places where the `on_failure_callback` is called. This leads to two incorrect behaviors. 

1. The `on_failure_callback` is incorrectly called when a task has retries and goes in `UP_FOR_RETRY`

2. The `on_failure_callback` is sometimes called twice

### What you think should happen instead

The on_failure_callback should only be called once when the task goes into a failed state.

### How to reproduce

These two patches (https://github.com/eejbyfeldt/airflow/commit/b0e7a0ae3b2c494bb75772866466110c6b3b7e8f, https://github.com/eejbyfeldt/airflow/commit/c48ca448ac3419d7b2d840405ed0b4699b8ccc02) modifies and existing test case to show that it now in correctly and the second one adds a test case showing it now gets called more than once.

                 python_callable=task_function,

That change does not look correct to me. The current condition that determines if the on_failure callback is called is
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/699171679a79917e9c2ee798f71a01d3051f3cc4/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1895
So the correct condition for deciding the callback would need to replicate that logic? 

Also not reraising the exception seems very problematic to me. The reason it currently called twice is that after reraiseing we end up here
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/699171679a79917e9c2ee798f71a01d3051f3cc4/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1465-L1479
which handle updating the state and running the failure fallback. Just swallowing the exception like in the patch you posted will result in the task being incorrectly marked as success.

Seems to me the reason for us not calling the `on_failure_callback` on cases where the task was externally marked as success/failed is this branch:
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/699171679a79917e9c2ee798f71a01d3051f3cc4/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1468-L1475
so it seems like the correct fix would be to call the callbacks from there. Because that is the bug that PR was aiming to solve right? Or did I misunderstand the goal?

It seems incorrect to me that assuming SIGTERM is the same thing being marked failed externally. As SIGTERM can be received for other reason, like the pod-preemption when running on k8s, and for such cases we want to go through the normal failure handling code.

On further debugging, I realized why the failure callback was not being called when tasks are terminated externally. It's because the state of the task instance was already marked as failed so it runs this: https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/b65dbaaf3f21ea5396da121bbfa7f895d0ab8516/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1471-L1475 instead of https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/b65dbaaf3f21ea5396da121bbfa7f895d0ab8516/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1476-L1479

We can use flag to signify when we have a sigterm but it needs testing to ensure the behaviour is desired due to this:
> It seems incorrect to me that assuming SIGTERM is the same thing being marked failed externally. As SIGTERM can be received for other reason, like the pod-preemption when running on k8s, and for such cases we want to go through the normal failure handling code.

Here's my implementation which you can test and give me feedback:

    Fix failure callback when task is terminated externally
    
    The previous fix caused the callbacks to be called even on task retries.
    On debugging, I found that the AirflowException was actually caught but because the task instance
    was already in a failed state, the failure handler was not called.
     To fix this, I introduced a flag to signify that sigterm occurred so that it's handled
    properly.

What I did was to revert the previous commit and introduced a flag

Seems the previous PR wasn't supposed to be made! https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/b65dbaaf3f21ea5396da121bbfa7f895d0ab8516/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L1468-L1470

What do you think @ashb, @potiuk

I do not have a lot of time to look at this in detail but from the quick view and speed with which we got the report (thanks @eejbyfeldt ) I think we should revert it for 2.5.3. And think about potentially improving the callback mechanism in 2.6 or beyond. Part of discussion on the new SLA proposal  (https://lists.apache.org/thread/kn1rb9l70jk16j83fycp68l2g70wnhzl) is about potential of making changes for all the callbacks (including the proposed sla callback) following much more "at-least-once" [delivery semantics](https://wiki.cantara.no/display/architecture/At-least+once+semantics) in a more "systematic" way - because we have loosly "at-most-once" now it seems coupled with some buggy cases where we have "not-even-once" semantics :D. 

Also dragging attention of @pierrejeambrun and @jedcunningham and @eladkal .

We already have quite a few fixes merged for 2.5.3 it looks, so I would be personally (also following our "release-early/release-often" discussion) be for reverting that one and releasing 2.5.3 - maybe even in a week or so. Possibly with some more scrutiny and attempts to better diagnose some of those issues that we've been regularly moving from milestone-to-milestone - there are a few of those - likely important - that seem to be perpetually in the "next" bugfix release.  Happy to join the efforts :).
